qualification: local A05.4 generated compare-exchange page-fault recovery acceptance; not all atomic helpers, hardware, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidate.acceptedBoundary: The generated direct compare-exchange helper publishes its BLR continuation PC only when its typed result is DORY_JIT_ATOMIC_RESOLUTION_PAGE_FAULT. The existing instruction side table and active write checkpoint then identify and restore the faulting atomic instruction.
candidate.failClosedBoundary: Compare-exchange fallback and error results do not publish a recovery PC. Exchange, fetch-add, general locked RMW, bit-test RMW, and pair compare-exchange still retain their prior conservative exit paths.
candidate.priorNegativeEvidence: The earlier broad checkpoint experiment included this one compare-exchange PC publication but was confounded by a missing CALL-terminator checkpoint and one atomic-isolation host signal. This retry runs on top of the accepted terminator-safe checkpoint foundation.

verification.focused: 59 tests in the ABI, metadata-fault, and restartability suites passed.
verification.deterministicAggregate: 1,552 tests in 179 suites passed with test parallelism disabled; the environment-driven pinned boot test skipped because its variables were absent, then the same pinned inputs were executed explicitly.
verification.targetedCoverage: A real MAP_JIT absent-page compare-exchange proves exact side-table ownership, an active checkpoint, preserved entry RFLAGS, and preserved RAX.

disposition.reason: The status-specific MAP_JIT proof and two independent clean runs crossed both prior failure modes, four aggregate code-cache wraps, all seven authenticated workloads, and clean ACPI poweroff.
disposition.remainingA05_4Work: The other four generated atomic helper families require page-fault-specific PC publication, focused coverage, and production reliability evidence before the atomic class and A05.4 can close.

limitations: Two passing local runs are a bounded reliability check, not cross-host qualification.
The production fixture proves overall reliability but does not assert that every generated atomic helper faulted during the runs.
This evidence does not satisfy the greater-than-95-percent dispatcher gate or G1-G5.
